page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual server in the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with Hyper-Threading. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and comes bundled with 384 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and features a 16 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets.

Benchmark results indicate moderate performance across standard workloads. The server achieves average tier results in stress-ng single-core (2411.16) and multi-core (8740.87) evaluations, alongside an average Passmark CPU score of 7697.28. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak, measuring 35.47 GB/sec for reads and 17.49 GB/sec for writes. Computational tasks such as software compilation with Clang and image processing also fall into the weak performance tier, while text processing and ray tracing benchmarks maintain average ratings.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak database operations benchmark of 2003.37 in Passmark, this server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, and basic text processing rather than intensive database hosting or high-throughput LLM inference. It offers a cost-effective entry point for resource-dense storage needs due to its bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD, balancing moderate compute capabilities with a generous local storage allocation.
